PR-034 (script half).reason: pycore_service_uninstall runs disable -> rm unit -> daemon-reload -> stop --no-block last, so an uninstall started inside the pycore unit leaves nothing enabled even if the stop kills the script. pycore owns the systemd-run --scope half.

requirements section 2: server / at 0777.reason: The cause was not found in code (no path chmods a literal /), so the helpers are hardened. fs_perm_target_safety checks both the literal path and readlink -f against the system-path list, and repair_owned_tree_777, ensure_owned_tree_777 and repair_owned_entry_777 use it, so //, /., /www/.. and a symlink to / are refused (owner probe). The suggested read-only server check (ls -ld /www, readlink -f /www, stat of /) is recorded for the user.

requirements section 2: /remote-control.reason: Both launchers print 'run /remote-control <lead> in the lead once' when a remote role is configured and the running lead lacks --remote-control, and remote rows log the ssh form with the secret NAME (the target is never resolved or printed).

issues: scripts/shells/linux/common/fs_perm_helpers.sh:160 (non-blocking) the refused list covers / /usr /etc /bin /sbin /lib and exact /var, but not /home, /root, /boot, /opt, /srv, /mnt, /media, /tmp, /run, /proc, /sys, /dev, /lib64, /var/lib or /var/log. A misconfigured symlink to /home would still make every home dir 0777. Extend the list to those exact paths; /var/lib and /var/log also with subpaths, while keeping /var/_core_node allowed.
